extracted.intended_audience: professional photographers working in photojournalism and/or documentary photography considering or entering the World Press Photo Contest
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and judging criteria for entries to the 2026 World Press Photo Contest, including regional assignment, eligibility, prohibited content, what juries see at each round, jury structure, categories of winners, and prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional contest model
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 World Press Photo Contest adopts a regional approach, dividing the world into six global regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the entry process, entrants indicate the country/countries in which their work was shot. Entrants do not need to place work into a region themselves; the organisation will sort entries into the relevant region ahead of the judging process. The six regions were chosen to increase diversity while keeping regions a manageable size; no grouping is perfect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region assignment for multi-region series
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are judged in the region in which they have been taken; specific rules apply if a series includes photographs from multiple regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a majority of images are from one region, the project is automatically placed into that region. If there is no clear majority of photographs from one region, the entrant should indicate the region they prefer to have their entry judged in when entering on Picter. A full list of which countries fall into which region is provided in the contest materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on artificially-generated images
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of generative fill or fully generated images is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artificially-generated images (including fully generated images and generative fill) are not allowed under any circumstance and therefore cannot win the World Press Photo Contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — professional photographer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest is open to professional photographers working in the field of journalism and/or documentary photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants do not need a press card, but must provide a document with a valid date that confirms current professional status. A range of different documents is accepted because 'professional' is recognised as a broad term; details of acceptable proof are specified in the entry rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging structure (regional and global juries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are chosen by regional and global juries in a multi-stage process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional juries, each made up of five professionals from and/or working in that region, first prepare a selection of entries per region. From this selection, a global jury — consisting of the six regional jury chairs and the global jury chair — then award the winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information provided to juries by round
rubrics_metrics.description: Different amounts of photographer and project information are shared with juries at successive judging rounds to balance blind visual assessment and contextual evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round 1: No photographer information is given to ensure entries progress based on visual quality alone. From Round 2 onwards: the photographer’s nationality, where they are based, gender, title of the work and a short caption are provided. From Round 3 onwards: the longer caption is provided. From Round 4 onwards: additional information such as motivation, the type of project (assignment/personal project) and funding is provided. At no point is the photographer’s name or any other personal information shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason for sharing limited photographer information
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited photographer information is provided to help ensure representation and balance in the selection of winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be representative of the world, it is important that a percentage of photographers are local to the region they are photographing in; both local and external viewpoints are valuable. Providing limited information (but not the name) helps tackle regional and gender representation and results in a better selection while improving diversity across winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for global jury choosing regional winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional juries prepare selections, but the global jury chooses the winners to ensure a globally balanced set of stories and images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If regional juries alone picked winners, there is a risk that each region’s winners would be too similar across regions (e.g., forest fire images chosen for every continent), leaving other types of stories out. The global jury selects winners to showcase a selection of stories and images balanced across the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and categories of winners
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest awards a fixed number of winners across defined categories per region, plus overall prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There will be 42 winners in total: per region there will be three Singles winners, three Stories winners and one Long-Term Projects winner. Out of the 42 winning entries, the global jury will choose the World Press Photo of the Year and two finalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes and awards for winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Winning entries receive monetary awards, camera equipment, publication and exhibition exposure, and invitations to events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional winners receive €1,000 each. The World Press Photo of the Year winner receives an additional €10,000. Winners receive a Fujifilm X Half camera; the World Press Photo of the Year winner (and two finalists) additionally receive a FUJIFILM GFX camera and lenses. Winning work is included in the annual traveling exhibition (shown in 80+ cities), published on World Press Photo platforms, and included in the Yearbook. Winners are invited to a winners’ event in Amsterdam and receive a physical award.
